**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity), NONCOMPETE.**

**What I found**
- The document contains two clauses numbered § 12.4. The second (p0046) imposes a non-compete on *us*: "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory."
- This is walk-away territory: a post-term restriction of 24 months and an undefined scope ("any product or service that competes"). It also fails every fallback element — no named product, extends past the term, exceeds 12 months, and no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions.
- It directly contradicts § 12.3 (p0044), where Vendor acknowledges we "made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment" — cited in the redline comment.

**Locations checked and excluded**
- First § 12.4 (p0045) — no-hire/non-solicit covenant; a different rule, not double-flagged here.
- § 13.4 (p0051) — ordinary acceptable-use restrictions, not field-of-use or competitive.
- § 14.2 (p0054), § 24.2 (p0088), § 28.1 (p0103) — ownership, Vendor-side assignment limit, and governing law; no restriction on our business (§ 24.2 binds Vendor and benefits us).

**Redline (validated, ok:true)** — one surgical replace at p0046 taking the preferred position: the sentence now confirms we are subject to no non-compete or field-of-use restriction and may develop, market, sell, or acquire competing products in any territory. The comment offers the narrowed fallback (term-only, one named product, 12-month cap, development and acquisition carve-outs) if Cobalt needs protection.
